A.name: Instrument
A.blurb: One family for everything: IBM Plex Sans for UI, IBM Plex Mono for values, tags and times. Cool slate neutrals. Dense, 13px base.

fonts.mono: "IBM Plex Mono", ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, monospace

B.name: Almanac
B.blurb: Serif display (Source Serif 4) over a humanist sans (Source Sans 3), mono only for values and tags. Warm paper neutrals. 14px base.

fonts.mono: "IBM Plex Mono", ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, monospace

C.name: Hyperlegible
C.blurb: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next everywhere, its mono for values. Pure neutral greys, 15px base, 44px targets: the outdoor-first, gloved-hand answer.

fonts.mono: "Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono", ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, monospace

red.name: Red on black
red.blurb: Black surfaces, one long-wavelength red carried at four luminances. Nothing but red light leaves the screen.

ember.name: Ember
ember.blurb: Burgundy surfaces, dim red ink, amber for warnings and emphasis. Warmer and easier to read, at the cost of some dark adaptation.

sequential.note: Cover and heights. Comparability groups never share one ramp: each group takes its own step range and the separate-scales chip.
Accumulation, rate, wave height, sea state.
Speed and gust. Direction is a glyph, never a colour.
Relative and specific humidity, dew point, column vapour, boundary-layer height.
Inverted: the dark end is low visibility. Fog states are chips, not colours.
AOD and particulates; the indices in these families take the ordinal ramps instead.
Aurora probability and OVATION. Kp is ordinal; Bz is diverging.

diverging.note: Blue below freezing, red above. Neutral grey at exactly zero.
Southward (negative) Bz is the aurora-favourable side; blue keeps it distinct from temperature's red.
Positive omega is descent (warm brown); negative is ascent (teal).

ordinal.note: Canadian AQHI by health-risk category; the number is always printed. Eleven per-value steps cannot clear the ordinal lightness rule on the dark surface.
ECCC seeing and transparency indices, unlabelled integers 0 to 5.
